social_security.summary: Federal Social Security benefits are not taxed by Alabama.

public_pension.summary: Pensions from the Alabama Teachers' and Employees' Retirement Systems, Alabama police and firefighter systems, and federal civil service retirement annuities are fully exempt from Alabama income tax.
conditions: Applies to Alabama state retirement systems (TRS, ERS, Judicial), Alabama police and firefighter retirement, and U.S. civil service and other federal retirement funds

private_pension.summary: Payments from a private defined benefit pension plan are fully exempt; other taxable retirement income such as 401(k) and IRA distributions is taxable except that taxpayers 65 or older may exclude the first $6,000.
conditions: Defined benefit plan payments (IRC 414(j)) fully exempt
Defined contribution/401(k)/IRA distributions: first $6,000 of taxable retirement income exempt
$6,000 exclusion only for taxpayers age 65 or older

sources.quote: Beginning January 1, 1991, all payments made on or after such date to a retiree or his designated beneficiary under a “defined benefit plan,” as defined under 26 U.S.C. § 414(j), to the extent such payment would be taxable for federal income tax purposes.
a. Beginning January 1, 2023, the first six thousand dollars ($6,000) of taxable retirement income. b. This exemption may only be claimed by individual taxpayers who are 65 years of age or older.

military_retirement.summary: U.S. military retired pay and survivor benefits derived from it are fully exempt from Alabama income tax.

sources.quote: (d) Effective January 1, 1989, and for all successive tax years, all retirement payments or compensation recognized under this section shall be exempt.

notes: The agency page is a bulleted list of exempt income, so the page quotes are runs of consecutive list items rather than sentences. No section in lexflow's Alabama index expressly exempts Social Security (Alabama's gross-income definition in 40-18-14 never adopted IRC 86), so social_security has only a page source. The $6,000 age-65 exclusion (40-18-19(a)(13)) is on ADOR's Schedule RS and its instructions, but lexflow cannot read the text of those PDFs, so the private_pension page quote covers only the defined-benefit exemption. The index marks 40-18-19 'Amended by Act 2026-603, effective October 1, 2026'; the text quoted is the version the index carries (in force for tax year 2025), and the 2026 change has not been reviewed here.
